note: Project annotation, not part of the OMG XMI. Each rule is quoted from the cited Common Logic draft; the plain-language lines, the choice of core pieces and the rebuild formulas are this project's. scripts/cl_meaning.py checks every rebuild against the quoted rules.

source.title: ISO/IEC FCD 24707 Common Logic (CL): a framework for a family of logic-based languages, final committee draft
source.caveat: A public draft; the final ISO/IEC 24707:2007 and 2018 texts are licence-gated and were not consulted, so their wording or numbering may differ.

Equation.quote: true if I(T1) = I(T2), otherwise false
Equation.plain: True when both terms name the same thing.

AtomicSentence.quote: true if I(S) is in relI(I(P)), otherwise false
AtomicSentence.plain: True when the things named by the arguments stand in the relation the predicate names.

Negation.quote: true if I(C) = false, otherwise false
Negation.plain: True when its one component is false.

Conjunction.quote: true if I(C1) = … = I(Cn) = true, otherwise false
Conjunction.plain: True when every component is true (with no components, true).

Disjunction.quote: false if I(C1) = … = I(Cn) = false, otherwise true
Disjunction.plain: True when at least one component is true (with no components, false).

Implication.quote: false if I(C1) = true and I(C2) = false, otherwise true
Implication.plain: False only when the first component is true and the second is false.

Biconditional.quote: true if I(C1) = I(C2), otherwise false.
Biconditional.plain: True when both components have the same truth value.

UniversalQuantification.quote: true if for every name map A on N, I[A](B) is true; otherwise false.
UniversalQuantification.plain: True when the body is true whichever thing in the universe of discourse the bound name stands for.

ExistentialQuantification.quote: false if for every name map A on N, I[A](B) is false; otherwise true.
ExistentialQuantification.plain: True when the body is true for at least one thing the bound name could stand for.
